text:
maya: quick sketch — thinking about doing a shadow RAG run while using speculative decoding on the generator. goal: see whether speculation amplifies hallucination when retrieved context is noisy. plan: 1) baseline full decode, 2) speculative decode with fallback policy, 3) quantized 8-bit variant. Anyone tried RAG+spec before?

zach: I did a tiny pilot — speculation reduced latency ~25% but made answer drift when retriever included unrelated doc. need solid holdout sets. :thinking_face:

li: suggestion — use retrieval confidence buckets and measure factuality per bucket. also include length-conditioned bins.

sophia: agree. define metrics: exact-match on synthetic q/a, rouge/f1 on long answers, and an attribution score (are citations present and correct). also track fallback rate (how often speculation aborted).

maya: here's a draft eval command i ran locally:
```bash
python eval_rag.py --model ozma-mini-6.7b --speculative True --fallback_threshold 0.35 --quant 8
```

zach: sample output from that run (toy):
```
LATENCY p50: 320ms -> 240ms
FALLBACK RATE: 12%
FACTUALITY_EM: 0.74 -> 0.69
CITATION_HIT: 0.81 -> 0.62
```

li: those are big citation drops. could be due to prefetching the wrong spans during speculation. we should instrument KV cache provenance and retriever span alignment.

maya: proposal: run a 10k query holdout with 3 retriever noise levels (clean, mildly-noisy, adversarial), two model configs (full, speculative), two quant levels (fp16, int8). measure latency distribution, EM, citation_hit, hallucination_rate.

sophia: also add a 'speculation_conservative' config — low speculative beam size + higher fallback prob. tradeoff curve.

ops-bot: scheduled job created — rag-spec-scan/8032110001; will run on dedicated-ops pool, eta 6h. :robot_face:

zach: can we also capture token-level divergence stats (where speculative diverged from full decode) to analyze patterns?

maya: yes. i'll log first-200 divergent tokens and context windows. will post results in this thread. thanks all :)
